subject: SLO acceptance test plan, dry-run, and penalty scenarios
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@orionhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: SLO acceptance test plan and penalty scenarios - request

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement and R&D Ops at Orion would like a single deliverable we can include in the contract appendix: a detailed acceptance test plan that our engineering team can run (dry-run), and a clear table of penalty/credit scenarios tied to measured SLO failures.

Specifically we need:
- A step-by-step test plan (scripts, input profiles, expected pass/fail criteria).
- Measurement methodology (how you compute availability and latency, sampling cadence, any probe types).
- Examples of how a service credit would be calculated for different classes of degradation (partial regional, total outage, elevated latency lasting N minutes).
- Artifacts from a representative dry-run (logs, aggregate results).

Can you provide a runnable spreadsheet and a one-page executive summary? We'd like to run the dry-run in our staging next week (preferred window Oct 26-28). If possible, include any preconditions or required IAM/network configurations so our infra team can prepare.

Thanks,

Anita Shah
Head of Procurement, Orion Health
anita.shah@orionhealth.com

--
Attachment: None in this message
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO acceptance test plan and penalty scenarios - request

Hi Anita —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is the draft acceptance test plan (SLO-Acceptance-Test-Plan-v1.3.xlsx) and an executive summary in the first tab. High-level notes:

- Test plan covers availability (service-level healthchecks + end-to-end request sampling) and p99/p95 latency windows at the route level.
- Measurement windows: we use 5-minute aligned sampling for availability (binary up/down probes) and 1-minute rolling windows for latency percentiles when the endpoint is healthy.
- Probe sources: synthetic probes from three AWS regions (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1) plus customer-supplied origin (your staging VPC) to account for network egress differences.
- Dry-run artifacts: we capture raw probe logs, aggregated histograms, and a short PDF summary (dry-run-results-20261022.pdf) after execution.
- Penalty matrix: included as a CSV (penalty-scenarios-matrix.csv) with example calculations for partial-regional degradation, total region outage, and sustained latency above threshold. Example rows show token-level normalization where applicable.

A couple of implementation caveats for the staging run:
1) Time sync: please ensure the staging host clocks are NTP-synced to avoid window misalignment (we mark windows by UTC minute boundaries).
2) Traffic shaping: if you want realistic client profiles, provide a saved request trace; otherwise we'll run our standard 95/5 read/write mix.

Next steps:
- We can do the dry-run Oct 27 09:00-11:00 PT if that works for your infra team.
- Karthik will follow up with the exact probe scripts and a short checklist for firewall rules/IAM.

Sending attachments now.

Regards,

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: SLO-Acceptance-Test-Plan-v1.3.xlsx (spreadsheet), executive-summary (first tab)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@orionhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO acceptance test plan and penalty scenarios - technical clarifications

Monica / Anita —

I reviewed v1.3 of the test plan and ran a short local dry-run against our staging harness. A few technical clarifications and suggested edits before you execute on Oct 27:

1) Sampling alignment: we recommend starting probes on the 00 second mark of each minute (we instrument token counts by minute). If your staging scheduler can't hit that granularity, use the included script with an initial random jitter and we will normalize on server-side ingestion.

2) Probe governance: the plan currently uses three synthetic regions. For crediting calculations where customer-origin vs public-probe divergence matters, add an extra column to indicate "customer-origin-only" probes — those will be weighted 1.5x for outage attribution.

3) Latency percentiles: we compute p99 from a 1-minute sliding window but bucket by the route's typical max context length. For long-context routes (>512 tokens) latency thresholds differ — I added route-level thresholds in the spreadsheet (tab: thresholds).

4) Penalty formula examples: the attached CSV demonstrates both time-weighted and request-weighted approaches. For contract simplicity we can publish the request-weighted example as the default (simplicity for audit); however if Orion prefers time-weighted (you care about duration more than volume), we should call that out explicitly.

5) Evidence packaging: we'll produce a single archive with raw probe logs, aggregated histograms, and a signed checksum. That archive is intended to be uploaded to the shared Drive link (see Monica's related_links).

Please see inline comments in the spreadsheet (column comments) — I put a few footnotes on threshold definitions and on-of-service edge cases (partial degradations that last <5 minutes).

I'll be available during the dry-run window to help interpret results.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Serving & Reliability, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks Monica and Karthik —

This looks good. Procurement reviewed the acceptance plan and R&D Ops reviewed the technical clarifications Karthik added. Two small items before we sign:
- For the penalty formula, we prefer the request-weighted example for the contract (simpler to audit).
- Please add a one-paragraph note in the executive summary describing how synthetic probes differ from customer-origin probes and how that affects crediting.

If you can update the spreadsheet with those two changes, procurement will route the contract to legal and we will request signatures via DocuSign. We can proceed with the dry-run Oct 27 09:00-11:00 PT — I've tentatively reserved that window.

Best,

Anita Shah
Head of Procurement, Orion Health
